# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Respondents → the public account each story is based on

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What would have made a difference

whys.g1: All three answers say the daily log isn't the problem and the schedule (with subs, RFIs, safety) is what eats the day, so one group named 'Holding the schedule is the real job' is how a super would sort them and the name is plain.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line; all three are on-topic replies about what matters on the job.

whys.g1: All four answers say the log isn't the problem because holding the schedule (subs, crane, RFIs, safety) is the real job, so one plainly named group is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on the line; all four are on-topic replies about why the log isn't where the time goes.

whys.g1: Two answers with different reasons (the day's slipping schedule pushes the log to morning; pour-day noise drowns out talking into a phone) are rightly left on their own, since no group exists that either belongs in and pairing them would blur two separate problems a super would tell apart.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line; both are real job-site reasons that get in the way of the log.

founder.order_why: It runs from where the idea applies, to the problem, to my solution and how it fits, beats and gets adopted, to the pilot and the send, which is how I'd explain Fresco to a superintendent.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 4 show the same kicker and the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), so from the flow alone they read as the same screen twice.
founder.missing: What it does better (screens 13-14) gets no 'What do you believe is true?' screen, while fit (12) and getting started (17) each get one. For Fresco that belief is the whole bet: supers finish the log during the walks instead of hours in the trailer, about 90% faster.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking whether I could have talked over the site noise comes before I've been asked anything about how I actually capture notes on my walks, and the 'take short videos and talk over them' question should come before asking whether Fresco would have made things better, since that's the idea I'm judging.
PRIMARY.missing: How long it took me to get the photos and notes into the log and how I do it today (typing in the trailer at end of day, uploading to Procore), and whether the log ever got used in a dispute or delay claim with the owner.

screens.why3: I know what my supers do on a site walk and what they'd balk at, so I can pick the riskier step from what I've seen in the field.
screens.why4: The two options are the two steps I wrote, they don't overlap, and they're in my own words; recording on the walk versus reviewing before send is the real choice.
screens.why5: The belief and the bar say what I'd bet on, that supers will narrate short videos during walks, and nothing drifted from my mechanism.

screens.why1: Right after the last solution check and before anything goes out, a stop that says what locking will do belongs exactly here.
screens.why2: "The pilot" reads to me like the paid pilot on one site I'm asking contractors for, not a trial run of the study, and "freezes your beliefs" is Keel's word, not mine, so I read it twice.
screens.why3: It's my own study and my own decision to lock it; I know everything it asks of me.
screens.why4: A card to read with a Continue button; there are no options to judge.
screens.why5: Nothing I typed is restated or changed, and nothing of the product leaks to respondents from a founder-only screen.
screens.instead: Before strangers see it: try the study yourself first. Locking keeps what you believe as it is now and writes the questions superintendents and contractors will get. [Try it first] [Lock and write the questions]

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out, choosing who runs the interviews is the natural last setup step after the pilot.
screens.why2: "Who asks the questions" is clear, but "Keel's credits" and "Lock and record the interviewer" are Keel's own jargon, not a contractor-tech founder's words, and need a second read.
screens.why3: It is my own decision as the founder about how my study reaches supers, so I can answer it from what I know.
screens.why4: A preselected face to lock is a workable choice, but the screen doesn't plainly set the AI interviewer against me asking myself, and "lock and record" is an odd label for that choice.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes my problem, my solution or my roles; it only sets who delivers the questions.
screens.instead: Who will ask your questions? -- The AI interviewer (uses Keel credits; the link goes out by text) / I'll send the link myself and they answer on screen

screens.why1: Once I've said who asks the questions, picking how my superintendents answer is the obvious next step before the link goes out.
screens.why2: "More than 90% in loud places down to 5 dB" makes me stop: 5 dB is near silence, not a loud jobsite, so I can't tell what the figure means, and "Hear it" runs straight into "needs Keel's credits".
screens.why3: I know my supers answer from a loud site or a trailer at the end of the day and tap on a phone, so I can pick from what I know.
screens.why4: The three choices are complete and distinct, but the AI option's accuracy claim is garbled, which makes that option hard to weigh against text.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco leaks into the choice, and "Text only" keeps what I picked.
screens.instead: How should they answer? — AI interviewer (a face on video asks each question aloud; they answer by talking or tapping; it catches nearly every word in a quiet trailer and most words over site noise like a running generator) · Text only (they read each question and tap) · Let them choose (they pick when they open the link)

screens.why1: Last screen before sending, so choosing who gets the link is the obvious final step.
screens.why2: 'Someone I know' is plain, but 'People from a dataset: from what Keel found on Contacts' makes me read twice: what dataset, and whose Contacts?
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending this to supers I've met on site walks or want Keel to find them for me.
screens.why4: The two choices are distinct, but the second is vague, and there's no option to paste a list of supers' numbers or emails or to post one open link to a GC's crew.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco or its roles leaks here, and my pick, each super by name, is kept.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? — Supers I know, each by name (you send it) / A list I paste in (names and phone numbers) / Superintendents Keel finds for me (from its contact lists)

screens.why1: A screener asking which system I keep my jobs in makes sense up front for a study about getting the day's photos and notes into the daily log, though the kicker's 'A recent time' doesn't match a question that isn't about any time.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are plain to me, but nobody says a company 'runs on' Procore; it's the job, and the daily log is what's in it, so I'd read it twice.
screens.why3: I know what my jobs are on because I'm in it every day uploading photos and filling the log.
screens.why4: Yes and No miss the common case: we're on Procore on most jobs, but the owner makes us use ACC or their own system on one, so 'some jobs' is a true answer with nowhere to go.
screens.why5: The founder meant superintendents whose jobs run on Procore or ACC, and moving it to 'your company' drifts it from my job to the office's software decision.
screens.why6: It's short, one question, and saying 'A-C-C' aloud is fine for anyone in commercial building; two options are easy to hold.
screens.instead: On the job you're running now, do you keep the daily log in Procore or ACC? Yes, Procore or ACC; No, something else.

screens.why1: After asking whether we run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I actually did the daily log this week is the obvious next gate before asking about the last one.
screens.why2: Entering photos and notes into the log is exactly what I do at the end of every day, so I'd answer on first hearing, though I'd call it the daily log or the dailies.
screens.why3: Doing the daily log is my own job every working day, so I know the answer straight off.
screens.why4: Yes and No are fine, but a gate takes no escape, and I get two chips: 'I'd rather not say' isn't an allowed escape, and 'I can't recall one particular daily log' makes no sense for a yes-or-no about this week.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's 'photos and notes still have to go into the daily log' and leaks nothing about a product.
screens.why6: One short question ending 'Yes or no' is easy to hear once and answer, and the chips aren't read aloud.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you put the day's photos and notes into the daily log yourself? Yes / No (no escape chip on the gate)

screens.why1: I've just said I put photos and notes in the log this week, so being shown an idea for that job before part two makes sense.
screens.why2: Site walk, assignees, due dates, action items, Procore and ACC are all words I use every day on the job.
screens.why3: It describes my own site walk and my own daily log work, so I can picture it from what I actually do.
screens.why4: A card to read with no options.
screens.why5: It is shown on purpose as an idea to imagine, says what it does in my terms, and nothing of the founder's own labels for me leaks through.
screens.why6: The middle sentence says three actions in one breath, and one of them is a list inside a list (photos, assignees and due dates), so it is a mouthful to hold when heard once.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco. On your site walk you take short videos and talk over them. Fresco turns them into notes with photos, who's on it, and when it's due. It texts each person their items. One click sends the notes to Procore or ACC. The people building it believe it would turn your walk videos into finished notes without you typing them up.

screens.why1: After an idea card that only says "Imagine Fresco" it's plausible this is about talking my log into a phone, but nothing told me that, so being asked about talking over site noise comes out of nowhere.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but "heard clearly" by whom (the owner's rep, my foreman, a phone?) needs a second read before I know what I'm answering.
screens.why3: I know how loud my site gets, but I type my last daily log in the trailer at the end of the day, not out on the deck, so I'd have to guess which moment you mean.
screens.why4: Yes easily, mostly, only sometimes or no covers it cleanly, and "I can't tell" fits if I don't know what I'd be talking into.
screens.why5: It quietly assumes I'd be speaking the log into something without the screen saying so, so the founder's voice idea leans on me rather than being put in front of me.
screens.why6: Two short sentences, one question, four short options and one escape, easy to hold when heard once.
screens.instead: Think of your site walks yesterday. If you spoke your notes into your phone as you walked, could it have picked you up over the noise? Yes, easily; Yes, mostly; Only in quiet spots; No. Or say I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, asking whether it would have made my last daily log better is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but "Fresco" is just a product name to me, and the options mix a better-or-worse scale with two specific benefits, so I'd have to read it twice.
screens.why3: I did a daily log this week, so I can say whether it would have saved me the evening upload hours or not.
screens.why4: "Hours back at the end of the day" and "Action items to the crew the same day" are both kinds of "It would have made things better", so three options overlap and I can't pick one cleanly.
screens.why5: "Hours back" and "action items to the crew the same day" read like the founder's pitch lines dropped in as answers rather than words I'd use about my log.
screens.why6: Five options can be held, but hearing "better", then two benefit phrases, then "no difference" is confusing by ear because the list doesn't run one way.
screens.instead: Thinking of your last daily log, would Fresco have saved you time getting the photos and notes in, or not? Saved me a lot of time; saved me a little time; no difference; cost me more time; or I can't tell.

screens.why1: After asking whether Fresco would have helped, it makes sense to ask whether I'd actually shoot videos and narrate them on my walks instead of snapping photos.
screens.why2: Taking short videos and talking over them on a site walk is plain to me; I already walk with my phone out all day.
screens.why3: I do the walks every day and know whether I'd stop to record and talk on a loud deck with gloves on, so I can answer from my own routine.
screens.why4: The four cover it, but the scale leans to yes: there are two yeses (one conditional) against 'probably not' and 'no', with no plain 'probably', and 'Yes, if it was clearly worth it' half-overlaps with 'Yes'.
screens.why5: It names Fresco only on the idea card and describes what I'd do in my own terms, so no product talk leaks into the question.
screens.why6: Heard aloud, the opening 'Take short videos and talk over them' sounds like an order before the question arrives, so it takes two sentences where one would do; the options themselves say fine.
screens.instead: On your site walks, would you take short videos and talk over them instead of photos, or not? Yes / Probably yes / Probably not / No -- or say I can't tell.
